deities: Manguesh (Mangesh, an incarnation of Shiva worshipped as a Shiva linga)

history.dynasty: Maratha (patronage); relocation by the Saraswat community
history.period: Deity shifted 1560 CE; present structure Maratha-era, rebuilt/renovated 1890 and 1973
history.summary: The Mangesh linga originated at Kushasthali (Cortalim) in Salcete on the banks of the Zuari river. After the Portuguese captured Salcete in 1543 and began Christian conversions in 1560, the Saraswats of the Vatsa and Kaundinya gotras shifted the linga to Mangeshi in Priol village of Antruz Mahal (Ponda), then ruled by the Hindu Sonda kings. The present temple was built under Maratha rule about 150 years after the shift (c. 1744 per some sources); Peshwa Sardar Ramchandra Malhar Sukhtankar, a devotee of Mangesh, had the village of Mangeshi donated to the temple in 1739. It was renovated twice during the Maratha period, again in 1890, and in 1973 a golden kalasha was fitted atop the tallest dome. Mangesh is the kuldevta (family deity) of many Goud Saraswat Brahmins. According to legend, Shiva manifested as a tiger to frighten Parvati; her cry 'Trahi Mam girisha!' (save me, lord of mountains) became 'Manguirisha' or Manguesh. The complex includes a large water tank (believed its oldest part), a seven-storey deepa stambha, a Nandi bull, sabha mandapa, agrashalas and a wooden chariot.

name: Shri Mangeshi Temple
town_description: Mangeshi is a village in Priol, Ponda taluka, North Goa (PIN 403404), about 21 km from Panaji on the Panaji–Ponda road (NH 4A). It takes its name from the Shri Mangeshi Temple, one of Goa's largest and most visited Hindu shrines, and functions largely as a temple town with pilgrim lodging (agrashalas), shops and restaurants around the temple complex. The CSV town 'Mangeshi (Priol)' combines the village with Priol, the nearby larger settlement; the temple stands at Mangeshi village itself.

travel.road: About 21 km from Panaji and 12 km north of Ponda on the Panaji–Ponda highway; well connected by bus and cab
